classified.text: MRI showed a 72×45×50-mm lobulated mass arising from the left iliopsoas muscle.

classified.text: The MRI mass is sharply marginated.

classified.rationale: It reports a signal characteristic on MRI.

classified.text: The MRI mass shows marked postcontrast enhancement.
classified.rationale: It states an imaging finding after contrast administration.

classified.text: These imaging features strongly support a calcified soft-tissue neoplasm centered in muscle.
classified.rationale: It draws a diagnostic conclusion from the imaging features.

classified.text: The patient denied trauma.

classified.text: The leading differential is extraskeletal osteosarcoma of the iliopsoas.
classified.rationale: It states the clinician's leading diagnostic consideration.

classified.text: Extraskeletal osteosarcoma fits a painful deep soft-tissue mass with calcifications or ossification.
classified.rationale: It explains why the diagnosis matches the presentation.

classified.text: Extraskeletal osteosarcoma fits marked enhancement and constitutional symptoms.
classified.rationale: It links imaging and systemic findings to the diagnosis.

classified.text: Extraskeletal osteosarcoma is a malignant mesenchymal tumor producing osteoid in soft tissue without attachment to bone.
classified.rationale: It defines the disease entity.

classified.text: The imaging description of an intramuscular calcified mass with no osseous involvement is highly compatible with extraskeletal osteosarcoma.
classified.rationale: It connects imaging findings to the diagnosis.

classified.text: A second consideration is myositis ossificans.
classified.rationale: It states another differential diagnosis.

classified.text: Myositis ossificans can present as a calcified intramuscular mass.
classified.rationale: It describes a known clinical/radiologic feature of the condition.

classified.text: Myositis ossificans can present with pain on motion.
classified.rationale: It states a recognized symptom pattern.

classified.text: Myositis ossificans is less likely because there is no trauma history.
classified.rationale: It uses the absence of trauma to reduce the likelihood of the diagnosis.

classified.text: Myositis ossificans is less likely because the course is prolonged with systemic symptoms and weight loss.
classified.rationale: It explains why the clinical course argues against the diagnosis.

classified.text: Myositis ossificans is less likely because the lesion is described as a lobulated enhancing mass rather than the more typical zonal peripheral ossification pattern.
classified.rationale: It compares imaging patterns to argue against myositis ossificans.

classified.text: Another differential is synovial sarcoma or another soft-tissue sarcoma with calcification.
classified.rationale: It states an additional differential diagnosis.

classified.text: Synovial sarcoma can occur near joints in younger to middle-aged adults.
classified.rationale: It describes a known epidemiologic/clinical feature.

classified.text: Synovial sarcoma may calcify.
classified.rationale: It states a recognized imaging feature.

classified.text: Synovial sarcoma can be painful.
classified.rationale: It states a recognized symptom.

classified.text: The lesion is specifically arising from the iliopsoas muscle.
classified.rationale: It states the anatomic origin of the lesion.

classified.text: The lesion contains amorphous calcifications suggestive of osteoid matrix.
classified.rationale: It interprets the calcifications as indicating a specific tissue matrix.

classified.text: These findings make extraskeletal osteosarcoma a better fit than synovial sarcoma.
classified.rationale: It compares findings to favor one diagnosis over another.

classified.text: Tumoral calcinosis is less likely.
classified.rationale: It states a differential diagnosis is less likely.

classified.text: Tumoral calcinosis can present as calcified periarticular masses.
classified.rationale: It describes a known feature of the condition.

classified.text: Tumoral calcinosis is usually composed of lobulated calcific deposits without this pattern of enhancing intramuscular soft-tissue tumor.
classified.rationale: It contrasts typical imaging features to argue against the diagnosis.

classified.text: Tumoral calcinosis is not typically associated with weight loss or progressive pain from hip flexion.
classified.rationale: It links the absence of typical systemic/mechanical features to lower likelihood.

classified.text: Calcific myonecrosis is also unlikely.
classified.rationale: It states another differential diagnosis is unlikely.

classified.text: Calcific myonecrosis is unlikely given the absence of remote trauma history.
classified.rationale: It uses history to argue against the diagnosis.

classified.text: The combination of chronic progressive hip pain localized to the iliopsoas, constitutional symptoms, a sharply marginated enhancing intramuscular mass with amorphous calcifications, and no bone involvement most strongly supports extraskeletal osteosarcoma arising in the left iliopsoas muscle.
classified.rationale: It synthesizes findings into a diagnostic conclusion.
